tier_reason: The README (benchmark_url) gives only first-party absolute throughput ('peak performance around 100 millions instructions per second', 'tens of millions instructions per second on a modern CPU') and an unnamed 'way faster than the best alternatives'; no benchmark code, corpus, compiler, flags, CPU model or competitor numbers exist in the repo. The only ratios against named assemblers (100x SjasmPlus on CPCWiki, 30x 'best challenger' on the Haiku depot listing) are snippet-only, first-party-style claims, so C (numbers without methodology).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'peak performance around 100 millions instructions per second', 'tens of millions instructions per second on a modern CPU', 'way faster than the best alternatives' (no alternative named in the speed claim). CPCWiki RASM page (WebSearch snippet only, page unreachable here): '1 million lines in 0.03s on a modern computer, 100x faster than SjasmPlus'. Haiku depot package description (snippet only, page unreachable): '30 times faster than his best challenger'. The two multipliers disagree and neither has a published harness.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 167 stars, 21 forks, 638 commits; README lists Arkos Tracker, R-GX, RetroDev, PiStudio (Norecess) and the CPCSyntaxError emulator as built on or embedding RASM, plus an online playground (cpc-playground.iiivan.org)
corrections.caveats: No benchmark script, input corpus, hardware, compiler flags or competitor version is in the repo (top-level tree shows only sources, makefiles and build scripts). The README's speed claim names no alternative; SjASM, SjASMPlus, VASM, Pasmo, UZ80, BASM and ORGAMS appear only in a 'other assemblers you could try' list, not as measured baselines. The 100x SjasmPlus ratio (CPCWiki) and the 30x 'best challenger' ratio (Haiku depot) are snippet-only and contradict each other. SjasmPlus's own README claims '1 million lines by 2-3 seconds on modern computer', so 100x compares two self-reported numbers (derived from page data and snippet). 'Instructions per second' is not directly comparable with lines per second. The peak figure may assume the mimalloc build ('make superfastmi'), which the README says gives significant improvements on Linux; unstated which build was timed.

notes: Real, active (last commit 2026-10-06), MIT-licensed Z80 assembler with notable retro-scene adoption, but its speed claims are first-party absolute throughput only, with no harness and no named baseline on the repo page; keep at C with the 'no reproducible comparison, conflicting snippet-only multipliers (100x vs 30x)' shortcoming. CPCWiki (cpcwiki.eu), rasm.wikidot.com docs and depot.haiku-os.org all failed DNS here (ENOTFOUND), so their wording is from WebSearch snippets only. License, last_commit, maintenance_status and usability in the record are correct.
